exists: wf task list|done|cancel|supersede|progress (wflib/tasks.py, CLI in wf.py)
per-task generation (uuid4) and rev; done/cancel/supersede/progress must quote the current generation
done requires a non-empty result note
--evidence: a file inside the project (recorded as relative path and sha256) or a bare 64-hex digest
secret-pattern check on evidence text and resolved paths
does_not_exist: no claim or lease action: a task cannot be claimed exclusively by an executor or card
evidence is not bound to commit, tree, command, interpreter, environment, exit code, count or duration
a bare 64-hex digest is accepted without verifying what it digests
no cross-machine or platform attestation of who ran what
development cards (A/B/C, G1, D1, this card) are not wf tasks; they are tracked in conversations and PRs
records in this contract are documentation, not machine-verified evidence
task_protocol.rule: do not describe task claim/done as an evidence protocol until such a protocol is implemented and tested

test_environment_rules: run as a non-root user; root makes permission-failure cases pass or fail for the wrong reason
run in an isolated session (setsid); one observed run was terminated by a process-group signal
use an interpreter without startup .pth hooks (setuptools distutils-precedence.pth makes C2b audits fail closed); the interpreter found as python3 on PATH matters, not only sys.executable
use a private interpreter path and record its tree digest before and after each run; a shared /opt path was replaced by another actor during this review
bind every record to commit, tree, command, interpreter digest, exit code, count, duration and log digest

tier_r_contract.behavioural_checks: synthetic stand-in config and pin, allowed synthetic platform_verified decisions, block verdict, synthetic re-pin
tier_r_contract.update_rule: re-review tier R against the changed harness, regenerate with tier_r_contract(), update TIER_R_CONTRACT in the same commit naming the reviewer
tier_r_contract.child_boundary: in-process audit hook, not an OS sandbox: refuses the child's own writes outside the root and any launch except git (same resolved executable) and host/bin/runner.py, host/bin/verifier.py; os.system/fork/forkpty refused; whitelisted processes are not audited; deliberate bypass via ctypes or private modules is out of scope

event_sequence_policy.core: core.event saves state (seq+1) under the state lock, then appends the event; a kill in between leaves state ahead; core may continue writing, leaving an internal gap with state=max

consumers: live.check only on trees where it routes through _capture_inputs (PR32+, exec events with install_exec)
live.syntax_only: live._strict_log accepts duplicates; it is not the integrity check

event_sequence_policy.rule: fail closed: without verifiable recovery evidence a gap is unknown, never authorized; do not relax to strictly increasing plus state=max (indistinguishable from deleted manual history); never reorder, renumber or repair logs
